claims.claim: For n=22m, the stated coloring has 11m even color-1 elements, 5m odd color-2 elements, and 6m odd color-3 elements.
claims.evidence: Among 1,...,22m there are 11m evens. The color-2 odds comprise the 4m odds at most 8m and the m odds in (20m,22m], totaling 5m. The odds in (8m,20m] number 6m and have color 3. These intervals are disjoint and exhaust all odds.
claims.search_method: Direct exact interval-cardinality calculation, supplemented by exhaustive integer enumeration for m=1,...,48.

claims.claim: Rainbow triples with one even and one odd addend are in two-to-one correspondence with pairs consisting of one color-2 odd and one color-3 odd.
claims.evidence: Given differently colored odds u and v, set a=min(u,v), z=max(u,v), and e=z-a. Then e is a positive even integer in [22m], so it has color 1, and (a,e,z) and (e,a,z) are two distinct rainbow triples. Conversely, a mixed-parity Schur triple has an odd sum; its even addend has color 1, forcing its odd addend and odd sum to have colors 2 and 3. Those two odds uniquely recover their pair and their difference uniquely recovers the even addend. Thus every pair has exactly two ordered orientations and every such triple occurs once.
claims.search_method: Constructed and proved mutually inverse pair/triple maps, then checked set equality and fiber size two by exact enumeration for m=1,...,48.

claims.claim: The number of mixed-parity ordered rainbow triples is 60m².
claims.evidence: There are (5m)(6m)=30m² pairs containing one color-2 odd and one color-3 odd. The verified two-to-one correspondence gives exactly 2·30m²=60m² ordered triples.
claims.search_method: Exact product count using the proved correspondence, supplemented by exhaustive enumeration for m=1,...,48.

claims.claim: The number of odd-odd ordered rainbow triples is 39m²+3m.
claims.evidence: An odd-odd sum is even and hence color 1, so rainbowness requires one addend of each odd color. A high color-2 odd is at least 20m+1, while a color-3 odd is at least 8m+1, making their sum exceed 22m. The remaining addends are 2i-1 for 1≤i≤4m and 8m+2j-1 for 1≤j≤6m. Their sum is at most 22m exactly when i+j≤7m+1. The number of unoriented pairs is 6m(m+1)+(3m-1)(9m)/2=(39m²+3m)/2. Since the differently colored addends are distinct, each pair has two orientations, yielding 39m²+3m.
claims.search_method: Complete integer lattice-point count with endpoint checks, supplemented by exhaustive enumeration for m=1,...,48.

claims.claim: The coloring has exactly 99m²+3m ordered rainbow Schur triples.
claims.evidence: The addend-parity cases are exhaustive. Mixed-parity triples contribute 60m² and odd-odd triples contribute 39m²+3m. In the even-even case both addends and their sum have color 1, so no triple is rainbow. The disjoint total is therefore 99m²+3m.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive parity decomposition followed by exact addition; independently enumerated all ordered Schur triples for m=1,...,48.

claims.claim: This sequence has limiting rainbow density 9/22 and refutes the target with ε=1/220.
claims.evidence: The total number of ordered Schur triples is Σ_{x=1}^{22m-1}(22m-x)=binom(22m,2)=242m²-11m. Thus the density is (99m+3)/(242m-11), whose limit is 99/242=9/22. Indeed, exact cross-multiplication gives 22(99m²+3m)-9(242m²-11m)=165m>0. Since 9/22=90/220 while 2/5+1/220=89/220, every positive m violates the proposed bound. For every candidate N, choosing m with 22m≥N supplies such a violation, so the target's quantified upper bound is false.
claims.search_method: Exact normalization, leading-coefficient limit, rational cross-multiplication, and explicit negation of the asymptotic quantifiers; also checked by integer enumeration for m=1,...,48.
claims.witness: For every m≥1, take n=22m and color evens 1, odds at most 8m or above 20m color 2, and the remaining odds color 3; with ε=1/220 its rainbow count exceeds (2/5+ε)binom(n,2).

target_evidence: The exact target explicitly permits a rigorously verified counterexample sequence. The draft supplies one for every n=22m, and the independent parity analysis proves its exact rainbow count is 99m²+3m out of 242m²-11m ordered Schur triples. Its density tends to 9/22 and is, for every m≥1, strictly greater than 9/22>2/5+1/220. Because multiples 22m are unbounded, this disproves the target statement with the single fixed ε=1/220 and correctly negates the required eventual-for-all-n assertion. Hence the counterexample alternative fully resolves the entire requested target, the final headline is established, and the draft's claimed_resolution of FULL is ACCURATE.
